_comment: The pairs the version pins rest on, one per guardrail. `policy_digest` is computed by tests/test_guardrail_pin_tracks_policy.py over the enforced policy in the synth snapshot; `description_digest` is what the CDK put in that guardrail version's description. They are taken over different material and will never be equal - the invariant is that NEITHER CAN MOVE ALONE. A policy change with a frozen description means the version resource will not be replaced, so `cdk deploy` reports UPDATE_COMPLETE while the gateway keeps enforcing the previous published version. That is ADR-024's failure arriving through the mechanism built to prevent it, and the Platform Engineering seat reproduced it with a one-word edit and 24 passing tests. Update BOTH values of a pair, after re-synthesising, in the PR that changes that policy.
_shape_changed_at: ADR-063. This file held a single pair while the stack grew a second guardrail. The flat `policy_digest`/`description_digest` keys became `pairs`, keyed by the same names `PAIRS` uses in the test. The main pair's two values are BYTE-IDENTICAL to what the flat form held - ea66d6da36fe and 71d7e4767fa3 - which is the evidence that ADR-063 added a guardrail and changed nothing about the existing one's policy.

main._what: beaconpave-gateway. Every model call transits it, and it keeps its topic policy.
main.guardrail_version_at_pin: v4 is deployed from this pin; unchanged by ADR-063

tool_output._what: beaconpave-tool-output (ADR-063). The same policy with TopicPolicyConfig omitted, applied only to the tool-output channel. Its digest covers the same POLICY_BLOCKS list, and TopicPolicyConfig resolves to null in it - deliberately, so a topic policy appearing on this guardrail moves the digest and republishes the version.
tool_output.guardrail_version_at_pin: not yet deployed; this pin is the policy that publishes v1 when ADR-063 deploys
